A1.justification: Both complete 13-page PDFs describe the same Perturbation Forgery work. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original detection experiments, mask ablations, and runtime measurements in Tables 2–6, plus CIFAR-10 results and sensitivity analyses in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these original detection experiments, ablations, runtime measurements, and appendix results.

M1.justification: Noise-distribution perturbation, saliency/GradCAM/Sobel masking, pseudo-adversarial sample generation, and binary-detector training remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the method equations retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet100, CIFAR-10, Makeup, CelebA-HQ, and LFW with the same gradient-based, GAN-based, diffusion-based, and physical attack scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within corresponding Tables 2–4, 6, and 7. The adversarial detectors, synthetic-image detectors, and face-forgery comparison methods are unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain AUC evaluation, the 4/255 perturbation budget with unrestricted-attack exceptions, 1,000-image gradient-attack evaluations, and ten training epochs. Appendix preprocessing, victim models, and attack configurations also match.

E4.justification: The mask ablations in Table 5, t-SNE analyses in Figures 3 and 7, parameter and attack-intensity studies in Figures 4–5, and visual examples in Figure 6 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting in the result tables and appendix plots is unchanged. There are no revised run-count or seed disclosures, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings match throughout. For example, Table 2 retains the proposed method's PGD AUC of 0.9912, Table 6 retains 4.85 seconds for 100 images, and appendix Table 7 retains all CIFAR-10 scores.

T1.justification: Definition 1, Theorem 1, Gaussian assumptions, open-covering reasoning, and the appendix proofs of Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about noise-distribution proximity, open covering, and efficient model-agnostic detection of unseen gradient-based, generative, and physical attacks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of sparse masking and parameter sensitivity remain unchanged. Both versions acknowledge the difficulty of selecting optimal distribution-perturbation scales and the need for experimental tuning.

D1.justification: v3 adds a page-1 'Code at' footnote identifying the authors' PFD repository, which v2 lacks. Implementation settings, hardware, preprocessing, and existing baseline-resource links are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, Table 1 positioning, and novelty statements match. Different reference-page breaks do not represent additions or removals.

P1.justification: v3 adds the short code-access footnote, renumbers subsequent resource footnotes, and updates the arXiv version/date text. Main prose, terminology, and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 has additional vertical spacing, and text reflows across columns and pages, including the conclusion's ending moving onto page 8. Figures and tables retain their content, captions, and display structure.

improvement.justification: The new code-access footnote provides an implementation pointer absent from v2, modestly improving reproducibility guidance. Scientific evidence and explanations are unchanged, and layout shifts have little effect on readability. The supplied PDFs do not establish the linked repository's contents or functionality.
